sections.h2: Ways to sell in Hurst, TX
sections.html:
Three routes exist: an agent listing, a private sale, or a direct purchase for cash. Your choice turns on repair needs, debt against the house and your deadline.

Hurst is a compact suburb in the northeast corner of Tarrant County, north of Fort Worth near State Highways 121 and 10. The city has almost no raw land left, so nearly every sale involves an existing house with some age on it. That favors owners who can show the house well. It also leaves room for a direct sale when a roof, foundation or kitchen would cost more to fix than a listing would recover.

  • Agent listing: widest exposure, but showings and repair requests after inspection.
  • For-sale-by-owner: no listing fee, but you handle contracts and title paperwork.
  • Cash buyer: fewer steps, usually a shorter timeline, and no repairs.

sections.h2: Why so many Hurst houses are from the postwar years
sections.html:
The town boomed in the 1950s and 60s. After Bell Aircraft announced a helicopter plant in 1951, residents voted 36 to 24 to incorporate. North East Mall opened in 1972, Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport in January 1974, and the population was above 27,200 by 1970.

That boom explains why many Hurst houses are fifty to seventy years old. Older houses can carry original wiring, plumbing and slab issues, and buyers will price those in. The city footprint has barely changed since, so you are selling in a mature neighborhood with established trees and close access to employers on both sides of the Trinity River.

Hurst, Euless and Bedford share a school district. Name the district and the nearby highways in your listing, since buyers search by both.

Before you list, call the City of Hurst to confirm that any permits for completed work, such as a remodel or a fence, were closed out. A permit left open can slow a buyer's lender.

sections.h2: Which office bills a Hurst homeowner?
sections.html:
Hurst sits in Tarrant County, so the county Tax Assessor-Collector handles collection. The main office is at 100 E. Weatherford Street in Fort Worth, the phone is 817-884-1100, and eight branch offices serve taxpayers.

The county tax page offers a property tax estimator, a list of important tax dates and delinquent tax sale information. A truth-in-taxation database shows what each taxing unit has proposed for a given parcel. Treat the city, county and school figures separately when you read a bill.

A bill still open after January 31 goes delinquent on February 1. Here is how the charges build.

Late-payment charges on Texas property tax bills
TimingCharge
February 1Six percent penalty plus one percent interest
Each month after, through JunePenalty grows one percent a month, interest one percent a month
July 1Penalty becomes 12 percent
When an attorney is engagedUp to 20 percent more

Interest never stops at a ceiling. A lien attaches each January and can be enforced against the house after a sale, so unpaid tax worries a buyer's title company as much as it worries you.

sections.h2: What if I am facing foreclosure on a Hurst house?
sections.html:
Lenders in Texas mostly skip the courtroom and use the sale power written into the deed of trust. The clock runs in fixed steps.

  • A default letter opens a short window to catch up on missed payments.
  • A sale notice follows, posted at the courthouse and filed with the clerk three weeks before the auction.
  • Sales happen on a first Tuesday, and a Hurst house is auctioned in Tarrant County.

Federal rules usually hold a servicer back until a home loan is well past four months behind. A sale that closes first can protect equity and credit, so compare it with the other options and speak with a housing counselor or attorney.

Hurst deeds are filed with the Tarrant County clerk, who can quote the records charges for your instrument.

Homestead owners get a $140,000 school deduction and a ten percent yearly cap on appraisal growth, and seniors and disabled owners get an additional $60,000 for school taxes. Mention your exemption status in the sale materials so a lender can estimate the buyer's monthly cost.

Texas treats tenants and squatters differently. A tenant gets written notice to vacate, and the landlord goes to justice court if the tenant stays. A person who entered with no right at all can be handled through Property Code chapter 24B, which lets an owner ask the sheriff or constable for removal, unless the occupant is family or a past or present tenant or a suit is pending.

  • Eviction hearings come within a few weeks of filing.
  • A writ of possession follows only after a final judgment.
  • Wrongful removal can expose an owner to a lawsuit.

Speak with a Tarrant County attorney before filing the request.

sections.h2: Preparing a Hurst house for a quick closing
sections.html: Pull the deed, any payoff letter and the latest Tarrant County tax statement before you talk to buyers. Decide early whether you will repair, sell as-is or price for a buyer who plans to renovate. Compare written offers on closing date, who pays title costs and what happens if the inspection turns up work. A cash buyer can usually name a date within a few weeks, while a lender-backed buyer adds an appraisal and underwriting.

sections.h2: A step-by-step path from decision to closing
sections.html:
Begin by deciding which of the three routes fits. If you list, expect showings, an inspection and repair requests, then a lender timeline. If you sell privately, you write the contract and manage the title paperwork yourself. If you take a cash offer, the buyer usually skips repairs and the process is shorter.

Next, collect the deed, any payoff letter and the latest Tarrant County tax statement. Ask the title company to confirm that no liens or open permits are attached. Then compare written offers side by side, looking at the closing date, who pays closing costs and what happens when the inspection turns up work.

Finally, sign before a notary so the deed can be filed with the county clerk. Keep a recorded copy afterward.

A seller who is behind on taxes does not have to find the cash in advance. The closing agent can pay the balance from the proceeds, and the title company will want the lien cleared before it issues a policy to the buyer. Ask the Tarrant County tax office for a current statement so there are no surprises on the settlement sheet. If the house is a homestead, ask about installment arrangements before the July penalty step takes effect.

faqs.a: Tarrant County. Hurst is in the northeastern quadrant, just north of Fort Worth.

faqs.q: Whom do I contact about a Hurst tax bill?
faqs.a: The Tarrant County Tax Assessor-Collector, reachable at 817-884-1100 or at the Fort Worth office on East Weatherford Street.
A closing ahead of the auction can pay off the loan and end the process. Start early, because sale dates come monthly.

faqs.q: When does a Texas tax bill go late?
faqs.a: After January 31 in most cases. Penalty and interest begin on February 1.

faqs.q: Must I hire a lawyer to sell in Hurst?
faqs.a: Texas does not make you hire one, yet a lien, a probate matter or a foreclosure notice is a good reason to get legal advice.
